subject: Precision billing for chat slices & seat bundles
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@acmehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Precision billing for chat slices & seat bundles

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency and the Dedicated SKU options. Before we move procurement forward, we need clarity on a couple of subtle billing behaviors so we can map them to our budget models. Can you confirm how Redwood handles the following in practice?

1) Chat slices across context windows: when a single logical conversation exceeds the configured context window and is stored/served as two requests (windowA + windowB), are we billed separately for both windows (i.e., two full context charges) or is there a prefix stitching credit applied? We have many short bursts that occasionally exceed the window by a token or two.

2) Seat-bundle amortization: if we buy a 50-seat bundle (committed), but only 30 seats are active in month 1 and we have short-lived microburst users that generate tiny token counts, how are those micro requests charged relative to the seat commitment — are microburst tokens deducted from the commit first or billed on top until a threshold?

3) Rounding/minimums: do you round up token usage per request, per-minute, or per-billing-window? Do you use a quantum (e.g., 10-token minimum) and how does that interact with streaming responses?

We need sample invoice line items and a simple calculation we can include in our procurement packet. If you can attach a one-page worked example, that would be ideal. Also cc’ing our procurement lead Tom in case he has follow-ups.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Kim
VP Product, Acme Health
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Precision billing for chat slices & seat bundles

Sara — thanks for the clear list. I put together a short worked example (attached CSV) and wrote up our standard behavior plus the options we can offer for your pilot. High-level answers first:

1) Context splits (stitching): by default we bill each request based on its effective tokens (so if a conversation is split into two server requests, you are billed both). However, for committed Dedicated customers we offer a “prefix-stitch” credit where overlapping prefix tokens are not double-billed when they are detected as part of the same conversation within a configurable time window (default 1 hour). That credit is applied at invoice time and appears as a negative invoice line item.

2) Seat-bundle amortization: commit seats are converted to monthly compute credits (token quotas). Microburst traffic is first deducted from the committed token quota. If usage exceeds the monthly quota, overage tokens are billed at the overage rate. We can also create a small burst pool that does not decrement seat quotas (useful if you want to avoid exhausting commit for infrequent spikes) — it is priced as a small fixed monthly allocation.

3) Rounding/minimums: our baseline is a per-request quantum of 1 token with per-token metering (so minimal rounding). We provide an optional 10-token quantum for customers who prefer simplified invoicing (reduces invoice line noise). For streaming: tokens emitted as part of the same streaming session are aggregated and billed once the session completes or after an inactivity timeout.

Attachments: sample_billing_calc_20250729.csv (worked examples: small-chat-slice, stitch-credit, seat-amortization, burst-pool sample)

Next steps:
- I suggest a quick 30-min scoping call so we can agree whether you want prefix-stitch credits and whether you prefer the 10-token quantum for invoicing simplicity.
- If you opt into the prefix-stitch credit and burst-pool, I can add the pricing lines into a Mutual Action Plan draft for your procurement team.

Cc’ing Vanessa to confirm typical legal/PO implications (we sometimes need the M&A as an addendum for commit).

Best,
Evelyn Hart

Evelyn / Sara — quick internal note and confirmation:

- Stitch credit behavior described above is our standard for Dedicated customers but it requires the customer to enable “conversation affinity” in the config so the runtime emits the stitching metadata. That metadata is what allows us to apply the invoice-time negative line. Without the metadata we cannot safely detect prefix overlap across independent requests.

- Rounding: we do per-request precision (1-token) by default. The 10-token quantum is a billing-only abstraction and does not change meter-side enforcement; it simply aggregates small token usages to a minimum line-item size for accounting.

- Legal/PO: enabling stitch credits and a burst-pool typically shows up in the appendix (billing addendum) with the following items: how credits are calculated, dispute window (60 days), and a floor where credits cannot exceed 30% of the monthly commit in pilots. Karthik, can you confirm the 30% cap default and whether we can increase for strategic pilots?

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success — Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear explanation and the worked example — very helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement perspective: 

- We like the idea of a stitch credit but need the invoice example to show how it appears (line item name, negative amount, and whether it can push a month to net-zero for small pilots). Can you confirm the exact line item label and whether credits can exceed charges in a given month?

- Regarding the 30% cap on credits during pilots: Acme will need either no cap or a higher cap (50%) for the pilot because our traffic is bursty and we'd rather not be billed for early POC spikes. Is Redwood able to accommodate a higher pilot credit cap? If so, what would you need from us (commit size, term)?

- Finally, for seat-bundle amortization: can you provide the math for how commit -> token quota is calculated and an example showing a month where 20 seats are idle and we have 100k microburst tokens. We want to model both scenarios (microburst deducted from commit vs microburst billed as overage) for our CFO.

Proposed next step: if you're open, we'll accept a short MMP (mutual action plan) with the pilot cap and stitch credit toggles and target to sign by Aug 12. I attached our preferred MMP template to procurement email.

Thanks,
Tom Wu
Head of Procurement, Acme Health
